widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

HOW TO USE

Make a whole picture frame from one border pattern. The top row of nodes draws a border strip that repeats left to right. The rows below paint a corner that fits that strip, and Seamless Border Kit Pixaroma builds the frame from them: a 9-slice picture and the CSS line for website borders, the corner and one repeat of the strip for Photoshop or Illustrator, and a preview of the whole frame. Seamless Border Prep and Kit were sent to the pack by James, a Pixaroma user.

 Steps

  1. Describe the border's style in Prompt Pixaroma (1): the motifs, the colours and what it is made of, for example Spanish talavera ceramic tiles, deep cobalt blue bands, ochre and green floral motifs, cream glaze. The two Text Join nodes add the rest of the strip prompt and the corner prompt.
  2. Leave Sizes Pixaroma (2) on 1536 x 1536. The width of the strip is one repeat of the border.
  3. The seed (3) is on R, a new strip each Run. Like a strip? Switch it to F: the strip stays and only the corner is painted again on the next Run.
  4. Leave Seamless Tile Pixaroma (4) on Left and right: the strip repeats sideways only.
  5. Press Run. Read Show Text Pixaroma (which rows became the band): when it says WARNING, the border runs off the top or bottom of the strip picture and is cut there, so Run again for another strip.
  6. Two frames come out: the painted corner and the mitred one, with no model (a 45 degree join, like a picture frame). The Save Image nodes save the kit, the corner and the top strip of the painted frame. Like the mitred one better? Move the wires of those three Save Image nodes and of Show Text Pixaroma (CSS for websites) to the second Seamless Border Kit (mitred frame, no model).

 Writing the style

  • Write only the style in Prompt (1). The layout words (one band across the middle of plain white paper) are in Text Join Two Pixaroma (strip prompt = layout + style); change them only if the strip keeps coming out wrong.
  • The corner words are in Text Join Two Pixaroma (5. corner prompt = style + corner). Keep diagonal, tiled or meet out of them: those make the model draw a line along the join.

 Good to know

  • The corner KSampler (7) uses a new seed every Run, so you get another corner each time. Its denoise is 0.8: that paints an ornament on the turn. 0.9 and up can paint a bar along the diagonal; 0.7 stays close to the mitre.
  • repaint on Seamless Border Prep (6): Seam (the default) repaints only a band along the diagonal, so the strip's own rows carry on round the corner. Corner repaints the whole corner square, for a separate corner block. seam_width 0.4 leaves room for a bigger ornament; 0.25 makes a small one.
  • corner_at: Mirror line turns the corner where the pattern mirrors itself, so both halves of the corner match. The mitred frame then often looks like a designed corner on its own.
  • blend on Seamless Border Kit fades the last pixels of the corner into both strips, so every join matches exactly. Keep it low (8 to 16): more fades the strip into the corner.
  • For a website: save the kit as border.png and use the line in Show Text Pixaroma (CSS for websites). The inside of the box stays your page's own background.
  • In our tests the painted corners looked designed on tiles, baroque, Greek key and Art Nouveau borders. On loose styles (watercolour leaves, Celtic knots) the mitred frame was often the better one, which is why the workflow shows both.
  • The band is found by itself, also on parchment, plaster or a wall that is a different colour above and below. If the report shows the wrong rows, type the band's first and last row into band_top and band_bottom on Seamless Border Prep.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones (and an orange one whose model file sits in another folder on your PC).

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Models note. Shown as missing, but you have the file in another folder? Click the model name on the node and pick it.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Krea 2 Turbo) - The image model, Krea 2 Turbo from Krea: 8 steps, CFG 1. It paints both the strip and the corner.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 4B, reads the prompt) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the image model understands.
  • Load VAE (Qwen Image VAE) - Turns a finished render into a picture you can see, and a picture into the model's own format.

 The steps you set

Blue. These are the only nodes you need to touch; the numbered ones are in How to Use.

  • Prompt Pixaroma (1. describe your border's style) - The border's style only: motifs, colours, material.
  • Sizes Pixaroma (2. tile size) - The size of the strip picture. Its width is one repeat of the border.
  • Seed Pixaroma (3. fixed or random) - R makes a new strip each Run, F keeps the strip you like.
  • Seamless Tile Pixaroma (4. which edges join) - On Left and right: the strip repeats sideways. It changes the model AND the VAE, so the strip's VAE Decode takes the VAE from this node.
  • Text Join Two Pixaroma (5. corner prompt = style + corner) - Your style plus the words that ask for an ornament on the corner.
  • Seamless Border Prep Pixaroma (6. finds the band, lays out the corner) - Finds the border band in the strip, picks where the corner turns, and lays out a picture for painting the corner: the corner, the strip to its right, the strip turned down the side, and a mask.
  • KSampler (7. paints the corner, model WITHOUT Seamless Tile) - Paints the corner with denoise 0.8. It gets the model through Differential Diffusion, not from Seamless Tile: the corner must not wrap round.
  • Seamless Border Kit Pixaroma (joins and builds the frame) - Joins the painted corner exactly to both strips and builds the kit, the corner, the strips, the frame preview and the CSS line. The second Kit (mitred frame, no model) does the same with the corner Prep laid out, before any painting.
  • Switch Pixaroma (what to save) - Picks what Save Image Pixaroma saves from the strip: the strip itself, or the strip repeated the way Seamless Preview's view shows it.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves.

  • Krea2 Enhancer Pixaroma (sharper detail) - Gives Krea 2 sharper, bolder detail. On at 0.1, the setting of our Krea 2 workflows.
  • Model Attention Backend (faster attention) - Comfy Kitchen's faster attention. On a card where it is not available it uses the normal attention by itself.

 Helpers

Purple. They run by themselves.

  • Text Join Two Pixaroma (strip prompt = layout + style) - Puts the layout words in front of your style, so the strip comes out as one band across the middle of plain paper.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • CLIP Text Encode (reads the prompt) and CLIP Text Encode (corner prompt) - Read the strip prompt and the corner prompt.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt, one per KSampler. Krea 2 Turbo runs at CFG 1, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler needs one plugged in.
  • Empty SD3 Latent Image (blank canvas) - The blank canvas the strip is painted on.
  • KSampler (8 steps) - Paints the strip: 8 steps, CFG 1, er_sde, simple.
  • VAE Decode (uses the Seamless Tile VAE) - Turns the strip into a picture with the VAE from Seamless Tile, so its left and right edges join.
  • Differential Diffusion (soft mask edges), VAE Encode (normal VAE) and Set Latent Noise Mask (paint only the corner) - Get Prep's picture ready so the KSampler paints only inside the mask, with soft edges.
  • VAE Decode (normal VAE) - Turns the painted corner into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Seamless Preview Pixaroma (the repeat + seam check) - Shows the strip and checks its edges: PASS on Left and right is what you want. Up and down shows FAIL: a strip only repeats sideways. Its view is Tile (the strip on its own); click the view row for 2x2 or 3x3 to see it repeated.
  • Save Image Pixaroma (saves what you picked) - Saves the strip, in the same Seamless Borders folder as the frame pieces.
  • Preview Image (painted frame) and Preview Image (mitred frame, no model) - The two frames, to compare. They are made at most 4096 px wide.
  • Save Image (border kit, the 9-slice for CSS), Save Image (corner) and Save Image (top strip, one repeat) - Save the pieces of the painted frame at full size. Turn the corner 90 degrees for each next corner, and the strip 180 degrees for the bottom and 90 degrees for the sides (or wire the Kit's side_strip output to another Save Image).

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Show Text Pixaroma (which rows became the band) - Which rows of the strip Prep took as the border, and a WARNING when the border runs off the strip picture.
  • Show Text Pixaroma (CSS for websites) - The CSS line for a box with this border.
  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

", "buttonColor": "#f66744", "lineColor": "#f66744", "backgroundColor": "#2a2a2a", "info": {"title": "Nodes Info", "icon": "node-v5", "color": "#3d7cc9"}}

{"version": 1, "content": "

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers.

What runsTime
The whole workflow (strip + corner + both frames)about 30 s
The strip aloneabout 14 s

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models from disk (Krea 2 and its text encoder, about 18 GB together), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.
